the prevalence of anti-CCP antibodies in patients with chronic hepatitis C virus infection treated with pegylated interferon α2a was 2.4% (95% CI 1.2–5.0), which was significantly lower than the 5.5% (95%CI 4.5–6.6) prevalence in the general population.
the development of anti-CCP-positive rheumatoid arthritis following pegylated interferon-α2α treatment for chronic hepatitis C infection was observed in 3 of 5 patients.

the prevalence of anti-CCP positivity was significantly higher in patients treated with IFN-α than in controls (p = 0.001) and that this association was stronger in patients treated with pegylated IFN-α2a than in those receiving standard IFN-α (p = 1.0 vs. p = 0.002).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an anti-CCP-positive rheumatoid arthritis (RA) after pegylated interferon-α2α (PEG-IFN-α2α) treatment for chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection.
the development of anti-CCP-positive rheumatoid arthritis in a patient with chronic hepatitis C infection treated with pegylated interferon-α2α and ribavirin.
the development of anti-CCP antibodies and the onset of RA after treatment with PEG-IFN-α2a.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of pegylated interferon-alpha2a in the treatment of HCV infection does not increase the risk of RA.
pegylated interferon alpha-2a does not induce RA in patients with chronic HCV infection.
pegylated interferon-α2α is a risk factor for RA development, and the presence of RF or ACPA is not a contraindication to treatment with this medication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that pegylated interferon-α2A (Peg-IFN-α2A) therapy for chronic hepatitis C infection can lead to the development of anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (CCP)–positive rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and we have also provided evidence that the development of RA is associated with a specific HLA-DRB1 genotype.
we have shown that the development of anti-CCP-positive RA is a rare but real phenomenon following the treatment of chronic hepatitis C infection with pegylated interferon-α2A (PEG-IFN-α2a).
the anti-CCP antibody is a serologic marker for RA, and it can be induced by pegylated interferon-α2α (PEG-IFN-α2α).
The main takeaway from our work is that
pegylated interferon-α2 (Peg-IFNα2) treatment for chronic hepatitis C infection is associated with the development of anti-CCP-positive rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in a subset of patients.
the risk of RA in patients with chronic HCV infection is not increased by treatment with pegylated interferon-α2α (peg-IFN-α2a).

patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) who have a high level of anti–cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibody at baseline have an increased risk of developing erosive disease, regardless of whether or not they are treated with tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitor (TNFi) therapy.
